title: Sweet Noodle Kugel with Raisins and Cinnamon
summary: A sweet baked pudding of egg noodles and plumped raisins set in a creamy cinnamon custard, golden and crisp on top.
equipment: blender or large bowl and whisk

ingredients.item: fine salt for 4 litres of pasta water (0.5%)
ingredients.note: about 3¼ tsp; most of it goes down the drain

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Preheat the oven
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan) at least 20 minutes ahead, and brush the baking dish with 15 g of the melted butter.

steps.title: Cook the noodles
steps.text: Bring 4 litres of water to the boil with the 20 g salt and cook the egg noodles to the packet time, until fully tender - they won't cook any further once baked, so the custard simply sets around them.

steps.title: Drain over the raisins
steps.text: Put the raisins in a colander and drain the hot noodles straight over them. The heat and moisture from the noodles plump the raisins up as they sit.

steps.title: Make the custard
steps.text: Blend or whisk together the eggs, cottage cheese, sour cream, sugar, milk, cinnamon, lemon zest, salt and 40 g of the melted butter until smooth. Blending gives a silkier custard, while whisking by hand will leave soft curds of cheese running through it - either works, depending on the texture you want.

steps.title: Combine and assemble
steps.text: Stir the drained noodles and raisins into the custard, then spread the mixture into the prepared dish. Press down gently so most of the noodles are submerged, and drizzle the remaining melted butter over the top.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Set the dish on a rimmed baking tray and bake for 50-60 minutes, until the custard is fully set with no wobble in the centre (an instant-read thermometer should read 71°C) and the top noodles are golden and crisp in spots.

steps.title: Cool and serve
steps.text: Cool the kugel on a wire rack for at least 20 minutes before cutting, which lets the custard firm up enough to hold neat slices. Serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Drain the hot noodles directly over the raisins rather than separately - the residual heat and moisture are what plump the raisins, and skipping this leaves them tough.
Press the noodles down into the custard before baking so they're mostly submerged; noodles left sticking up dry out and scorch.
Check for a firm, wobble-free centre rather than relying on time alone, since oven performance varies - the custard should read about 71°C.
Let the kugel cool on a rack before cutting; slicing it hot causes the custard to collapse rather than hold a neat square.
storage: Keeps covered in the fridge for up to 4 days, or can be frozen in portions for up to 2 months. Reheat gently in a low oven or microwave until piping hot, or simply serve at room temperature. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
